title: Genesis
author: moses
attributionNote: Traditionally attributed to Moses. Modern scholarship treats Genesis as a composite work shaped by multiple authors and editors over centuries. The attribution is recorded as traditional, not established.
description: The opening book of the Tanakh, moving from creation and the first human families to the ancestral narratives of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph. This edition contains the complete book, from creation through the death of Joseph.
historicalContext: Genesis reached its present form in the Persian or early Hellenistic period, drawing on older traditions shared across the ancient Near East. Its creation language has close neighbours in Mesopotamian literature, while its theological claims are distinctive.
featuredNote: Creation, language and the ordering of the world
